subject: bowfin fish
title: This Fish Can Survive Five Days Out of Water. It Breathes Air

scenes.text: This fish can last about five days out of water.
The bowfin lives in swamps and slow rivers across eastern North America.
When the water turns warm and low in oxygen, it swims up and gulps air from the surface.
Its swim bladder works like a simple lung, so the air keeps it alive.
In droughts, bowfin can burrow into the mud and wait.
Its family has survived for more than a hundred and fifty million years. Every relative is extinct. Only the bowfin is left.

description:
The bowfin can gulp air at the surface because its swim bladder works as a primitive lung, and it can survive up to five days out of water.
It is the only surviving species of an ancient group of fishes that has lasted more than 150 million years.
What other living fossil should we cover?
first_comment: The male bowfin guards his young for weeks after they hatch. Have you ever caught one?
